Ryan Shea arrived in Edmonton from Pittsburgh this season and, 21 games in, The Hockey Writers is calling him the Oilers' number two defenseman. He's playing 23 minutes a night, and Oilers Nation has started comparing him to Darnell Nurse. That's a big jump for a 29-year-old who was a 2015 fourth-round pick and spent years in the AHL.

The points aren't there: five in 21, two in his last ten, and our range expects more. But the defense is the job, and it's going well. Edmonton takes 52% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, five and a half points better than without him.

There's a reason the Oilers took the chance. Evolving-Hockey had him 5th among 215 defensemen last season at 3.3 wins above replacement, though it also noted his results ran ahead of his chances, so some of that was hot shooting or goaltending. Somewhere between that number and a depth guy is the truth. On a team chasing a Cup, a reliable 23 minutes from a left shot is worth a lot.
